title: Tech Note: Managing and Encrypting 4D Data Files
author: Tai Bui, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: New data key / Discover data key / Register data key
DOM XML commands (catalog.4DCatalog manipulation in Project mode)

historical_commentary.text: Data file (.4DD) encryption introduced in 4D v18 is still the current, supported mechanism for at-rest table encryption and remains fully relevant; the AES + SHA-256 passphrase design and the MSC-based workflow described here are unchanged in spirit in modern 4D releases, though the ORDA/.provideDataKey() API has become the more standard programmatic entry point over the older 'Register data key' command as 4D has continued to push object notation as default.
related_updates: 4D data file encryption (AES/SHA-256, MSC Encrypt tab) remains a current supported 4D Server/4D feature with no major architecture change since v18

Project mode's catalog.4DCatalog XML manipulation trick for toggling 'Encryptable' programmatically is a project-mode-only technique; binary mode databases are increasingly rare as 4D has fully embraced Project Mode as the default going forward
Object notation (ds.provideDataKey()) is now the standard/preferred style over the classic 'Register data key' command form
